input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages—those MMS things—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Do you also need my date of birth, or is that enough?

I just checked, and it looks like my phone isn’t able to send MMS messages right now. As for using the internet with mobile data, I’m not sure how to check that—could you guide me through it? I get a bit confused with these things.
Yes, please go ahead and guide me through the test. I’d appreciate step-by-step help, since I get a bit lost with these things. Thank you!
I just ran that test, and it says my messaging app cannot send MMS messages right now. What should I do next?
I checked the status bar, and it shows the airplane mode icon is on. There’s also the battery icon at 80%. I don’t see anything about signal strength or mobile data. What should I do now?
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now the status bar shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” and the battery is still at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or mobile data icons. What should I do next?
I tried to turn on mobile data, but it still says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” in the status bar. I’m not seeing any change—no signal bars or data icons have appeared. What should I do now?
I ran the check, and it says there’s no SIM card detected in the phone. What does that mean? Is that why I can’t send picture messages?

I followed your instructions and reinserted the SIM card. Now the status bar shows a signal (though it says “Poor”), 2G, and “Data Disabled.” I checked the SIM status again, and it says the SIM card is active and working. What should I do next?
I turned mobile data on, and now the status bar shows a signal (still “Poor”), 2G, and “Data Enabled.” What should I do next?
I changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G. Now the status bar shows an excellent signal, 5G, and “Data Enabled.” What should I do next?
I just ran the test again, and it still says my messaging app cannot send MMS messages. What else can we try?
I checked the APN settings. The current APN name is “internet,” and the MMSC URL for picture messages is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Is that what it’s supposed to be? What should I do next?

I followed your instructions and reset the APN settings, then rebooted my phone. But I still can’t send MMS messages—the test says it’s not working. This is getting a bit frustrating. Is there anything else we can try? I really need to send these pictures.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned off on my phone. What should I do next?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it only has permission for “phone.” It doesn’t have permissions for storage or SMS. Could that be the problem? What should I do?

I granted both the storage and SMS permissions to the messaging app, but I still can’t send MMS messages—the test says it’s not working. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to worry I’ll never get this fixed.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Alternatively, I can guide you through a quick test on your phone to check the mobile data connection and MMS capability. Would you like me to proceed with that? If yes, please confirm, and I will start by checking your phone's MMS sending capability.

Thanks for confirming that your messaging app cannot send MMS messages right now. Let's proceed with some checks and fixes to resolve this.

First, we need to ensure your phone has proper cellular service and mobile data connectivity, as MMS requires both.

I will guide you through checking your phone's cellular service status next. Please run the "check_status_bar" diagnostic on your phone and tell me what icons or messages you see related to signal strength, airplane mode, and mobile data status.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
I checked the status bar, and it shows the airplane mode icon is on. There’s also the battery icon at 80%. I don’t see anything about signal strength or mobile data. What should I do now?

Since Airplane Mode is ON, it disables all wireless communications including cellular service and mobile data, which is why you cannot send MMS messages.

Please turn OFF Airplane Mode on your phone. This is usually done by swiping down from the top of your screen to access the quick settings panel and tapping the airplane icon to disable it.

After turning off Airplane Mode, please check your status bar again to see if you now have signal strength bars and mobile data indicators. Let me know what you see.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now the status bar shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” and the battery is still at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or mobile data icons. What should I do next?

Since you have "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," it means your phone is not connecting to the cellular network and mobile data is turned off.

Let's try turning mobile data ON. Please go to your phone's settings or quick settings panel and enable mobile data.

After turning mobile data ON, check the status bar again and tell me if you see signal bars and a mobile data icon (like 4G, LTE, 5G, etc.).

I tried to turn on mobile data, but it still says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” in the status bar. I’m not seeing any change—no signal bars or data icons have appeared. What should I do now?

Since your phone shows "No Signal" even after turning off Airplane Mode and enabling mobile data, there might be an issue with your SIM card or network connection.

Next, please run the "check_sim_status" diagnostic on your phone and tell me the result. It will indicate if your SIM card is active, missing, or locked. This will help us determine the next steps.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
I ran the check, and it says there’s no SIM card detected in the phone. What does that mean? Is that why I can’t send picture messages?

Yes, if your phone is not detecting a SIM card, it cannot connect to the cellular network, which explains why you have no signal, no mobile data, and cannot send MMS messages.

The SIM card is essential for your phone to access your carrier's network.

Please try the following:
1. Power off your phone.
2. Remove the SIM card from its slot.
3. Carefully reinsert the SIM card, ensuring it is properly seated.
4. Power your phone back on.

After doing this, check if the SIM card is detected by running the "check_sim_status" diagnostic again and let me know the result.

SIM card re-seated successfully.

Great! Your SIM card is now detected and active, and you have some signal, though it's currently on 2G.

Next, let's turn ON mobile data since it is still disabled.

Please enable mobile data on your phone again. After that, check the status bar and tell me if you see a mobile data icon like 2G, 3G, 4G, LTE, or 5G.

Mobile Data is now ON.

Thanks for enabling mobile data. Since your phone is connected to a 2G network, this could be a reason why MMS is not working properly, as 2G networks are generally not suitable for MMS.

Let's improve your network connection by changing your phone's network mode preference to allow 4G and 5G.

Please run the command to set your network mode preference to "4g_5g_preferred" on your phone. This will enable your phone to connect to faster networks if available.

Please run the "reset_apn_settings" command on your phone to reset the APN settings to the carrier's default.

After resetting, you will need to reboot your phone for the changes to take effect. Please reboot your device and then try sending an MMS message again.

I understand your frustration, and I'm here to help you further.

Next, let's check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your phone, as it can sometimes interfere with MMS.

Please run the "check_wifi_calling_status" diagnostic on your phone and tell me if Wi-Fi Calling is ON or OFF.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.

Since Wi-Fi Calling is off, it is not causing the MMS issue.

Next, let's check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS, such as access to storage and SMS.

Please run the "check_app_permissions" for the messaging app on your phone and tell me if it has permissions for "storage" and "sms."

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it only has permission for “phone.” It doesn’t have permissions for storage or SMS. Could that be the problem? What should I do?

Yes, lacking permissions for storage and SMS can prevent your messaging app from sending MMS messages.

Please grant the messaging app the necessary permissions by running these commands on your phone:

1. Grant "storage" permission to the messaging app.
2. Grant "sms" permission to the messaging app.

After granting these permissions, try sending an MMS message again and let me know if it works.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I granted both the storage and SMS permissions to the messaging app, but I still can’t send MMS messages—the test says it’s not working. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to worry I’ll never get this fixed.

Thank you for trying all these steps so far. Since your phone has good cellular service, mobile data enabled, correct APN settings, Wi-Fi Calling off, and the messaging app has the necessary permissions, but MMS still does not work, this issue may require deeper technical investigation.

I will transfer you to a human agent who can provide further specialized assistance.

Transferring you now.
